title: Grasp — a workout planner that shows its working
description: Grasp plans your session and works out the weights from what you actually lifted — then tells you why it picked them. Free on iPhone, works offline, no ads.
og_description: Plans your session, works out the weights from what you actually lifted, and tells you why. Free on iPhone. Works offline. No ads.
hero_lede: Grasp plans your session around your goal and your gym, works out the weights from what you actually lifted last time, and tells you why it picked each one.
store_aria: Download Grasp on the App Store
hero_meta: Free on iPhone, in 15 languages. No subscription, nothing to unlock.
lang_lede: The screens, the exercise names and their step-by-step instructions, not just the menus. Arabic reads right to left, the way it should.
plan_title: Your next workout, built for you
plan_body: Tell it your goal, how many days you train, how long a session is and what equipment you can actually reach. It will never suggest a movement you cannot do. Save a setup for every place you train, and switching gyms rebuilds today's session.
plan_alt: Grasp's workout screen: nine exercises planned for a full-body muscle-building session, each with its weight
equip_title: Tick what you have. It plans with nothing else.
equip_body: A few dumbbells at home, a full rack at the gym, a band in a hotel room: save a setup for each place and switch in one tap. Grasp only plans exercises you can do with what is ticked, and rebuilds today's session when you switch.
equip_note_home: Home: 5 of 58 pieces ticked, so every exercise is one you can do there.
equip_note_gym: Gym: everything ticked, so the whole library is open.
equip_note_tail: Over 50 kinds of equipment to choose from.
prog_title: Every weight comes with a reason
prog_body1: Most training apps hand you a number and leave you to trust it. Grasp shows the reasoning, and lets you disagree in one tap.
prog_ledger_why: Every set reached the top of your range — up 5 kg.
prog_body2: Hit the top of your rep range on every set and the weight goes up; miss it twice and it comes down. Five kilograms here because that is the smallest step the machine's stack has. Warm-up sets are worked out from your working weight, and the rest timer starts itself.
prog_alt: An exercise in Grasp: an animation of the movement, warm-up sets, and last time's weight
rec_body: A body map shades each muscle by how recently you worked it, so a week of training reads at a glance instead of needing to be added up. Muscles fade as they recover.
rec_alt: Grasp's body map, with the muscles trained today highlighted
vol_body: Sets are counted against a weekly target for each muscle group, and you can change the target. You can see where the week's effort went, and what is still short.
vol_alt: Grasp's weekly targets: sets done per muscle group against a target
int_body: Rope, sprints, planks: work and rest, counted for you, with a sound at every change so you can put the phone down. Save your own presets. Between sets, the rest timer rings and counts down in the notification shade.
int_alt: Grasp's interval timer with work, rest and round settings
log_body: Everything lives on your phone and works with no signal. An account only backs your training up so it survives a lost phone. Export everything as a spreadsheet or a complete backup whenever you want. It is your training, in a format you can open.
log_alt: Grasp's training log on a calendar
ai_p1: There is no language model deciding what you lift. Grasp's planning is ordinary, inspectable arithmetic: volume targets per muscle, a fatigue model based on what you logged, and a progression rule that fits in a sentence.
ai_p2: A system that guesses cannot tell you why it guessed, cannot be checked, and cannot run on a phone with no signal. This one can do all three.
final_lede: Free on iPhone. No ads, no subscription, nothing to unlock.
final_meta_html: On Android? Email {email} and we will tell you when it is out. Gyms and brands interested in working together, same address.
disclaimer: Grasp suggests training weights from what you log. It is not medical advice and it cannot see your form or your health. Talk to a doctor before starting a new training program, particularly if you have an injury or a health condition.
